strengths: Well-motivated problem identification through rigorous empirical analysis (Section 3) demonstrating concrete limitations of attention-based Top-K selection, particularly under text-vision granularity mismatch
Principled information-theoretic framework grounded in cognitive science principles (information foraging), with theoretical justification for greedy algorithm via approximate submodularity analysis

Comprehensive experimental validation across three diverse benchmarks (M3CoT, ScienceQA, LLaVA-W) and two model architectures (Chameleon-7B, Qwen2-VL-7B) in both 0-shot and 1-shot settings, with consistent improvements (up to 18% on LLaVA-W)

Extensive and rigorous ablation studies, component interaction analysis (Section 5.5), hyperparameter sensitivity analyses (Appendices K-L), complexity analysis, and deployment evaluation demonstrating scientific rigor
Synergistic design of three complementary components (CAG, AVP, DAT) that work together organically to address identified limitations
Thorough documentation with algorithm details, hyperparameter specifications (Table 5), and promise of code release supporting reproducibility
weaknesses: Limited novelty of individual components: CAG is straightforward context concatenation, information gain for selection is well-established, and DAT's attention-shift detection is a reasonable but relatively simple heuristic—novelty lies primarily in combination rather than novel methodology

Critical unvalidated assumption: the paper assumes reducing entropy on next-token prediction optimizes final answer quality, but no empirical evidence directly demonstrates this correlation, which is fundamental to AVP's validity

Significant computational overhead of 1.36× vs. ICoT (Table 8) due to K forward passes with lookahead; despite KV caching optimizations, this cost is non-negligible and could prohibit practical deployment

Substantially diminished improvements on stronger models: Qwen2-VL-7B shows only 1.1–6.2% gains vs. 4–18% on Chameleon-7B, raising serious concerns about scalability to larger/more capable models and suggesting the method may not generalize

Weak empirical support for DAT mechanism: correlation analysis shows r=0.2166 (p=0.048), barely meeting significance threshold, and only provides post-hoc analysis on baseline outputs rather than validating actual insertions in AIMCoT

Candidate set construction still relies on problematic attention maps for Cattn despite identifying their unreliability; random sampling for Cexp is simplistic with Appendix M showing minimal differences between sophisticated alternatives

Limited scope: evaluation restricted to VQA-style tasks; unclear generalization to image captioning, document understanding, or other vision-language tasks requiring different information-seeking strategies

Missing critical experimental rigor: no confidence intervals or significance tests on main results; some improvements modest enough to warrant statistical validation; multiple runs only for exploratory components

Hyperparameter sensitivity with multiple tunable parameters (N, M, K, δ, sr, sg) and non-negligible variation (0.23–0.30 ROUGE-L range for δ in Figure 5) without principled guidance for cross-dataset transfer
Absence of error analysis, failure cases, or qualitative examples of unsuccessful predictions that would illuminate when and why the method fails

strengths: Well-motivated problem with concrete empirical analysis of limitations in existing attention-based methods (Section 3, Table 1, Figure 1)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across three benchmarks, two VLM backbones, 0-shot and 1-shot settings, with extensive ablations and sensitivity analyses
Strong empirical gains on LLaVA-W benchmark (18.25% improvement in 0-shot), demonstrating effectiveness on challenging open-ended generation
Thorough complexity analysis and deployability investigation (Appendix J) with honest assessment of 1.15-1.36× computational overhead
Solid technical execution with well-described methods, detailed reproducibility information, and comprehensive appendices supporting main claims
weaknesses: Limited novelty: Each component represents incremental application of existing techniques—CAG is standard prompt engineering, AVP applies well-established greedy submodular optimization (Nemhauser et al. 1978), and DAT is straightforward attention monitoring

Weak empirical motivation: Masking experiment shows only 3.93% degradation (modest), single illustrative example is anecdotal, and attention-shift correlation is weak (r=0.2166, p=0.048). These are insufficient to justify fundamental critique of existing methods

Inconsistent improvements across settings: Gains are minimal on Qwen2-VL-7B (1.1-1.3%), modest vs ICoT on Chameleon-7B (1.4-5.5%), and concentrated on single benchmark (LLaVA-W). No clear understanding of when/why method works

Problematic computational trade-off: 18.25% improvement on LLaVA-W comes at 36% computational cost (8.58s→11.65s); improved gains across most settings cannot justify this overhead for practical deployment

Theoretical concerns: Information gain objective assumes model entropy equals task relevance (unvalidated); approximate submodularity only satisfied in 61-72% of cases (Table 6); no evidence that high-IG regions improve reasoning quality vs just being different from high-attention regions

Insufficient generalization and transfer analysis: Only tested on VQA tasks with two recent VLM architectures; no evaluation on other vision-language tasks or older models; hyperparameter tuning required per dataset (Table 5) raises generalization concerns

Experimental rigor issues: No statistical significance tests or confidence intervals on main results; fairness of baseline comparisons unclear (ICoT is concurrent work); no analysis of failure cases or when method underperforms

Overstated claims: Framing as 'active information foraging' lacks cognitive science grounding; 'human-like reasoning' unsupported by any human studies; 'training-free' belies significant hyperparameter tuning; 'fundamental limitations' overstates 3.93% masking degradation

Design choice justification incomplete: Random sampling for exploratory set lacks principled motivation; three separate mechanisms not jointly optimized; grid-based region construction not compared with alternatives; CAG's specific contribution to granularity mitigation unvalidated

Presentation issues: Method relies heavily on hyperparameter tuning (Table 5 shows different settings per dataset) conflicting with deployability claims; key design rationales and ablations relegated to appendices; dense paper attempting to cover too much ground

strengths: Compelling empirical motivation with concrete examples (Table 1, Figure 1) showing limitations of existing attention-based approaches
Well-structured framework with three complementary components (CAG, AVP, DAT) that are individually motivated and address distinct problems
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across three benchmarks (M3CoT, ScienceQA, LLaVA-W) and two backbones with both 0-shot and 1-shot settings
Thorough ablation studies (Tables 3-4) and in-depth empirical analyses (Sections 3.1-3.3) that validate design choices
Strong empirical results with up to 18.25% improvement on LLaVA-W and consistent gains across settings
Excellent reproducibility: promised code, detailed hyperparameters, complete implementation descriptions, and 14 appendices with extensive analyses
Practical efficiency analysis showing reasonable overhead (1.15-1.36x vs. baseline) with batch processing and KV-caching optimizations
Well-presented framework with clear visualizations (Figures 1-3) and logical flow of ideas
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: individual components use well-known techniques (prompt-based description generation, entropy-based information gain, greedy selection, attention monitoring); primary contribution is their combination
Myopic information gain formulation (Eq. 8) only measures entropy reduction for next token; lacks comparison with other uncertainty quantification methods or multi-step lookahead
Narrow evaluation scope: all benchmarks are VQA-style tasks with factual answers; generalization to image captioning, dense QA, or open-ended vision-language tasks unclear
Empirical submodularity only holds in 61-72% of cases (Appendix H), weakening theoretical justification for greedy algorithm
Incomplete statistical analysis: no confidence intervals, significance tests, or variance reporting; some improvements modest (e.g., 1.4% on Qwen2-VL-7B)
Unexplained empirical findings: non-monotonic degradation in Table 1 (top-20 worse than top-10), random sampling performing as well as sophisticated methods for C_exp construction (Table 11)
Multiple hyperparameters with dataset-specific values (Table 5) but limited sensitivity analysis beyond δ; unclear how to set for new datasets
DAT trigger mechanism relies on potentially unstable attention shifts; threshold δ is sensitive (Figure 5) with limited validation beyond LLaVA-W
CAG efficiency not thoroughly analyzed: requires generating additional descriptions; combined benefits over individual components not fully explained
Modest improvements in some settings (e.g., 1.4% on Qwen2-VL-7B M3CoT) raise questions about statistical significance and practical impact

strengths: Clear problem identification with strong empirical motivation (Section 3.1 demonstrating 75%+ of instances have IoU<50% between attended and crucial regions)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 3 benchmarks, 4 backbones, and both 0-shot/1-shot settings with rigorous statistical significance testing
Thorough analysis including component ablations, super-additivity analysis, robustness to adversarial noise (>95% rejection rate), and qualitative case studies
Multiple validation approaches: Semantic Hit Rate (65.2% vs 18.7% ICoT), GPT-4v preference (76-81%), and correlation analysis of attention shifts with generation quality
Solid theoretical grounding in Information Foraging Theory with mathematical justification for greedy submodular maximization
Practical deployment considerations with realistic analysis (1.36× overhead) and safety mechanisms to prevent hallucination propagation
Strong reproducibility: detailed hyperparameters, algorithm descriptions, promise of code release, extensive appendices
weaknesses: Limited novelty in individual components: CAG is prompt engineering, information gain is standard active learning, attention shifts are straightforward - contribution is primarily in combination rather than new techniques
Heavy dependence on CAG description quality creates a single failure point; while hallucination rates are low (1.9-5.8%), no systematic analysis of robustness to poor descriptions
Hyperparameter sensitivity requires per-dataset tuning (δ=0.5 for M3CoT vs δ=0.2 for others); adaptive strategy shows performance gaps (-0.1 to -0.4), limiting generalization
Modest improvements on stronger models (Qwen2-VL-7B: 1.1-1.4% on M3CoT/ScienceQA) with dramatic variance across backbones (1.4% to 18.3%), suggesting model-dependent effectiveness unclear
Theoretical justification incomplete: entropy reduction is assumed to correlate with task performance but not proven; no ablation comparing information gain to other selection criteria
Limited evaluation scope: restricted to VQA tasks; generalization to other vision-language tasks (captioning, scene understanding) unexplored; unclear if approach is broadly applicable
Computational cost (1.36× overhead) not fully justified given modest improvements on stronger models; multiple forward passes (NC × K) may be prohibitive for deployment
Greedy algorithm gap to global optimum not analyzed; no comparison to alternative selection strategies beyond Top-K attention
Missing error analysis: no investigation of failure cases, behavior on complex scenes, or systematic ablation of what types of questions benefit most from AIM-CoT

strengths: Clear empirical motivation with well-designed analysis (Section 3) demonstrating limitations of attention-based selection and static triggers
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 3 benchmarks, 4 VLM backbones, multiple settings with proper statistical significance testing
Consistent improvements across all configurations, though with varying magnitudes
Thorough ablation studies and supplementary analysis including hyperparameter sensitivity, robustness testing, and deployability analysis
Multiple evaluation perspectives beyond standard metrics (SHR, GPT-4v qualitative, case studies) providing multi-faceted validation
Well-motivated problem formulation identifying genuine limitations in existing I-MCoT approaches
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: CAG is straightforward prompt engineering, AVP applies well-established active learning principles (information gain/entropy reduction), and DAT uses intuitive attention monitoring. Each component is relatively incremental.

Weak theoretical justification: Approximate submodularity holds in only 61-72% of instances (Appendix I.4, p-values ~0.02-0.046), insufficient to justify greedy optimality. Information Foraging Theory connection appears post-hoc, justifying intuitive choices rather than driving novel designs.

Modest empirical gains with uneven performance: Improvements range 1-2% on stronger models (Qwen2-VL-7B: 1.1-6.1%) to higher on weaker ones. Many significant only at p<0.05, not p<0.01. Practical impact questionable for large models.

Computational overhead (1.09-1.36×) contradicts deployment-friendly claims. 36% slowdown on LLaVA-W is substantial for deployment, and complexity analysis shows O(K·NC·L·∆N·(N+K·∆N)·H) remains expensive.
Dataset-specific hyperparameter tuning required (δ=0.5 for M3CoT, δ=0.2 for others). Adaptive Z-Score strategy (Table 11) shows performance degradation, undermining deployment claims.

CAG module creates circular dependency: improvements partly from using the same model twice. Quality depends on model capability. Hallucination rates remain 1.9-3.5% even with constraints (Appendix L.1).

Information gain does not fundamentally solve selection problem: Uses the same model's entropy, so model bias persists. No rigorous proof IG outperforms attention for task-relevant selection beyond post-hoc SAM validation.
Weak validation of DAT mechanism: Correlation with performance is weak (r=0.2166, p=0.048). Group analysis (89% vs 50%) lacks rigorous statistical reporting (effect sizes, CIs, sample sizes unclear).
Limited experimental scope: Only VQA tasks tested; generalization to other multimodal reasoning, visual navigation, or other modalities unclear.
Missing error analysis: No discussion of failure modes, cases where method doesn't help, or inherent limitations.

strengths: Well-articulated problem motivation with clear formulation of 'what to see' vs 'when to see it' limitations in existing I-MCoT methods
Comprehensive experimental validation across three benchmarks and four diverse VLM backbones with proper statistical significance testing
Multiple complementary evaluation approaches including SHR analysis, GPT-4v blind comparison, and robustness testing against adversarial noise
Solid theoretical grounding in Information Foraging Theory with empirical validation of approximate submodularity
Thorough ablation studies across multiple backbones and extensive supplementary analysis demonstrating consistent improvements
Practical deployment considerations with quantified inference overhead (< 1.36×), adaptive thresholding strategy, and safety mechanisms
Training-free framework that operates on frozen VLMs without requiring model fine-tuning
weaknesses: Limited novelty of individual components: CAG is prompt engineering, AVP uses standard information gain, DAT is straightforward attention monitoring; contributions are incremental rather than fundamental

Theoretical gaps: approximate submodularity only empirically validated (holds 61-72% of time), connection between entropy reduction and task-relevant evidence assumed but not formally justified, no approximation guarantees for greedy algorithm

Strong model capability dependency: improvements vary dramatically by architecture (18.3% on Chameleon-7B vs 6.1% on Qwen2-VL-7B); unclear generalization and suggests method effectiveness is architecture-specific

Hyperparameter tuning burden: different δ values required per dataset, fixed thresholds outperform adaptive thresholding, multiple hyperparameters (K, N, M, NC) requiring configuration undermines 'deployment-friendly' claims

Limited evaluation scope: restricted to VQA tasks; generalization to other multimodal reasoning tasks (visual grounding, image captioning) unclear; no comparison with recent multimodal reasoning methods beyond ICoT
Modest improvements on stronger models (1-6% on Qwen2-VL-7B, 2-7% on Qwen2.5-VL-32B) raise questions about practical significance despite statistical significance
Evaluation methodology concerns: SHR using SAM masks as ground truth is indirect (object segmentation ≠ task-relevant evidence); only proxy-based GPT-4v evaluation without human validation
Missing analysis: no failure case discussion, no information gain vs. task performance correlation analysis, no breakdown of computational cost across components
